title: Quiet tier-2 retry: no visible browser, no retry on sign-in rejection
description:
Two related quality-of-life fixes for _refresh_cookies_from_browser:

1. The 3rd attempt currently flips to headless=False. In daemon mode there is nobody to look at the browser; the visible Chromium launch immediately SIGTRAPs every time, generates a macOS CrashReporter dialog, and never recovers. Pin headless=True for all attempts.

2. When _fill_credentials_on_find_page returns False because Apple's iframe stayed present after submit, Apple has already evaluated and rejected the request. Retrying within seconds is rate-limit fuel and never works. Signal rejection via a per-attempt flag and break out of the retry loop early.

Acceptance:
- No more CrashReporter dialogs on daemon failures
- After a sign-in rejection, _refresh_cookies_from_browser returns after one attempt
- Existing tests still pass
close_reason: Both fixes landed in PR #11

title: Capture screenshot and iframe content on tier-3 sign-in failure
description:
When the Apple sign-in iframe stays present after password submit, we currently log only a generic warning. Apple's iframe is cross-origin (idmsa.apple.com) so we can't see error text from logs. Add diagnostic capture:

1. Full-page screenshot to session_dir/failures/<label>-<ISO>.png
2. Iframe innerText extraction (Playwright frame API works for cross-origin)
3. Register page.on('dialog', ...) to log+dismiss any JS alerts that may be blocking the flow (the user observed a visible alert)
4. Call from _fill_sign_in_form, _fill_credentials_on_find_page, and _attempt_automated_login failure paths

Acceptance:
- A failures/ dir is created under session_dir on first failure
- PNGs and a small .txt sidecar (frame URL + extracted text) saved per failure
- Dialog handler logs any alert text and dismisses
- Existing tests still pass
close_reason: Diagnostic capture added in same PR (#11)

title: Add rotating file log handler to daemon
description:
Daemon currently emits logs only to stdout. The user runs it in a foreground terminal with no redirect, so when the daemon fails after ~10 hours (falling back to manual credential re-entry), there is no persisted log to audit the failure path (tier-2 browser re-prime vs. tier-3 auto-relogin vs. iframe rejection). Add a rotating file handler in main.py that writes alongside stdout — small, reversible change that makes the next failure diagnosable.

Acceptance:
- Daemon writes to weasley.log next to the script (or under session_dir)
- Log rotation (size or time based) so file doesn't grow unbounded
- Stdout logging is unchanged (still visible in terminal)
- Log path and level configurable from config.json with sensible defaults

title: Send Pushover notification on daemon auth failure requiring manual intervention
description: When the daemon detects that manual re-auth is required (session refresh exhausted, about to exit), it should send a Pushover push notification to alert the user. This ensures the user knows they need to run 'python main.py auth' to restore location tracking. Should use the Pushover API with user/app tokens stored in .env or config. Should also notify on other critical failures (e.g. repeated SQS publish failures).
close_reason: Implemented Pushover notifications and daemon abort after consecutive failures

title: Abort daemon after repeated auth failures instead of polling indefinitely
description: When the daemon exhausts all 4 tiers of session refresh (validate → browser re-prime → automated login → give up), it currently logs the error and sleeps, then retries on the next cycle. This means it keeps hitting Apple's servers every ~5 minutes even when manual re-auth is clearly required. The daemon should track consecutive auth failures and exit the process after a threshold (e.g. 3 consecutive failures), so it stops spamming Apple and requires the user to restart with 'python main.py auth'.
close_reason: Implemented Pushover notifications and daemon abort after consecutive failures

title: Handle Find page sign-in when main session is valid
description: When the iCloud session is valid but the /find/ page requires re-login, the code detects the sign-in page in _prime_findmy_cookie_in_context but doesn't attempt to fill credentials. This means Tier 2 fails and Tier 3 also fails because it checks sign-in on main icloud.com (which is fine) then delegates to _prime_findmy_cookie_in_context which hits the same sign-in wall. Fix: attempt credential fill when sign-in detected during FMIP priming.

title: Proactively refresh FMIP cookie before expiration
description: Rather than waiting for a 450 then recovering: (1) Track FMIP cookie age by recording timestamp when saving session. (2) Before API calls, check if FMIP cookie is older than threshold (e.g. 30 min) and preemptively re-prime. (3) In daemon mode, re-prime every N cycles rather than waiting for failure.
close_reason: FMIP cookie age tracking with 25min threshold and proactive re-prime before fetch

title: Make FMIP cookie re-priming more robust
description: The current _prime_findmy_cookie_in_context() is fragile. Improvements: (1) Add explicit waits polling context.cookies() in a loop with timeout for X-APPLE-WEBAUTH-FMIP to appear. (2) Log cookies before/after priming to confirm refresh. (3) Retry priming 2-3 times before declaring failure. (4) Add configurable headless=False flag for debugging.
close_reason: Poll-based FMIP cookie wait, retry loop, debug browser flag

This is foundational for debugging all other session improvements.

title: Add credential leak safeguards
description: Architectural safeguards: (1) Isolate credential access to single function in auth.py. (2) Never log credentials — add redaction for password fields. (3) Never include credentials in session JSON. (4) Short-lived variable lifetime — read, use, del immediately. (5) Audit .gitignore for session/, *.env, keychain exports.
close_reason: Audit confirmed no leaks; added keychain file patterns to .gitignore

title: Implement secure credential storage via macOS Keychain
description: Use keyring Python library to store iCloud credentials in macOS Keychain. Add keyring to Pipfile. Create a single isolated function in auth.py for credential access. Add CLI command (e.g. 'python main.py store-credentials') for initial setup. Credentials encrypted by macOS, protected by login password, cannot be accidentally committed.
close_reason: keyring-based credential storage with isolated module and CLI command

title: Implement multi-tier session refresh architecture
description: Replace binary 'one retry then give up' with multi-tier strategy: Tier 1 (existing): Re-send with existing cookies. Tier 2 (existing): Re-prime FMIP via headless browser. Tier 3 (new): Automated re-login using stored credentials. Tier 4: Fall back to interactive auth. Each tier escalates only when previous fails.
close_reason: Implemented tiered refresh: validate → browser re-prime → placeholder for auto-login → fallback

title: Implement automated re-login (Tier 3)
description: Programmatically enter iCloud credentials into sign-in form using persistent browser profile. Since device is trusted (YubiKey), no 2FA needed. Use credentials from macOS Keychain via keyring. Triggered when FMIP re-priming fails but before falling back to interactive auth. Handle edge cases: unexpected 2FA prompts, changed password, account locked.
close_reason: Tier 3 automated re-login via keychain credentials with 2FA detection and form filling
